transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card customer service. My name is Marcus. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi Marcus, I have a problem with a payment I made for some painting on my house that I'm really not happy with.
Agent: I can help look into that. May I have your full name and the billing zip code on the account?
Customer: Yes, my name is Rupert Calloway, and the zip code is 43210.
Agent: Thank you, Mr. Calloway. Could you tell me the business name, date, and amount of the charge you're referring to?
Customer: The company was Brightcoat Painting. They charged my card on September 9th for $2,400.00.
Agent: Thank you. Can you tell me more about what took place with Brightcoat Painting?
Customer: Well, they came out and did the exterior paint job on the house. When they finished, I walked around with the guy, told him it looked fine, and paid the bill with my card.
Agent: Okay, so you gave them permission to charge the card on that day after checking the work?
Customer: Right, I swiped my card right there on their portable machine. But now that it's been a few weeks, I just really dislike how it turned out.
Agent: What is it about the work that you're unhappy with now?
Customer: In different lighting, the tone looks completely different than what I expected, and the sheen looks patchy on the sunny side of the garage. I really just hate the way the house looks now.
Agent: Have you reached back out to Brightcoat Painting about this?
Customer: I did call them last week. The owner basically said I accepted the job and signed their completion sheet, so they wouldn't do anything unless I paid them another fee.
Agent: Did they offer any other options or send someone back out to look at it?
Customer: No, he said once the walk-through is done and payment is made, their job is closed.
Agent: So just to make sure I have all the facts down, you hired Brightcoat Painting for $2,400.00, approved the work and paid on September 9th, but you are dissatisfied with the appearance of the paint job after seeing it over time, and the painter declined to redo it without an extra fee.
